raw_response:
I farm the same 13.1 mu the way we have for years, wheat first and then maize after. I do not read those technical things, so I look at what my land did before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can safely spend. Last year, if I feed the wheat too little, it turns weak and yellow, and then the harvest drops hard. So for wheat I would rather not cut fertilizer too much. Water from the well costs money, though, so I will not irrigate too many times unless the season stays dry. After wheat harvest, the maize has to go in fast. That gap is short, so I will keep the field work simple, use the usual seed I can get in town, put on enough fertilizer to hold the yield, and depend mostly on family labor. Some people in my house work outside, so I cannot make a plan that needs too much hand work or too many extra trips to the field.

For wheat I will use enough fertilizer and three waterings if needed, because wheat gives me trouble fast if I save too much on inputs.
